newsitem.title: USA: MCA chief Biondi says Viacom did not violate pact.
newsitem.headline: MCA chief Biondi says Viacom did not violate pact.

text.p: MCA Inc Chief Executive Frank Biondi said on Tuesday he did not think Viacom Inc's ownership of MTV networks violated the terms of the company's cable television partnership with MCA.

In testimony at Delaware Chancery Court, Biondi, who was fired last year by Viacom Chairman Sumner Redstone, appeared to bolster Viacom's case against MCA, telling the court he did not think Viacom was detrimental to USA Networks operation.

Viacom, which owns Paramount Pictures, MTV and Nickelodeon, and Seagram Co Ltd, which owns entertainment and theme park concern MCA Inc., have been fighting for control of the cable partership. Each side has accused the other of violating the terms of their partnership agreement.

At issue in the case is whether Viacom's launch of "Nick at Nite TV Land" and Viacom's MTV network violate the terms of the partnership, which prohibits either company from operating or launching entertainment cable networks outside of the USA Network.
Viacom contends there is no breach of the partnership, that the partnership is working well and that MCA is trying to get control of USA Network "at an unfairly low price".
Biondi said Viacom's position that the MTV Networks were grandfathered in was "fair and rational" because the networks had no "practical economic impact on MCA as a partner".
"Were we to start an unrelated network we would do it through USA," Biondi said.
Biondi, testifying in the awkward position as a Viacom witness, acknowledged that MCA could have asked Paramount for a waiver to buy its own cable operations, but never did.
"There were no opportunities (for MCA) to pursue," he said in his first day of testimony.
In January, Redstone fired Biondi as his chief executive and in April waived a one year, non-compete employment agreement so Seagram's Edgar Bronfman Jr. could hire Biondi as head of MCA.

Viacom attorney Rodman Ward revealed in court that Biondi's contract was bought out for $15 million in cash over three years plus an unspecified number of stock options and $2 million in deferred compensation. Press reports said Biondi's five-year deal with MCA was worth an estimated $40 million to $75 million in salary, bonus and Seagram stock options.

Under cross examination by MCA attorney Ron Olson, Biondi said Redstone's memory was almost photographic but added that while Redstone's recall was indeed "extraordinary", it was also "selective...and extremely self-serving".

The characterization could undermine Redstone's testimony that in a September 1993 due-diligence meeting before Viacom's proposed acquisition of Paramount, he recalled no mention of the USA partnership's non-compete or exclusivity provision.
According to Biondi, it was at that meeting that Redstone first said the MTV networks were grandfathered in.
Biondi returns to the witness stand on Wednesday.
